_note: The fellowship's single source of truth. The council (council-of-elrond) reads this file to ARM the machine: it installs every pack whose tier is in defaultTiers, and offers the rest. The README's Credits section mirrors the same entries, in the same order. A pack cannot be installed unless it is credited there, and cannot be credited unless it is in this file — that is the point of the file. Add or remove a pack in both places; `check-docs.mjs` fails when the table and this manifest disagree.
_where: This file lives inside the council-of-elrond skill on purpose. The skills CLI installs `skills/<name>/` and drops repo-root files, so a manifest at the repository root would not survive `npx skills add`. It ships here, with the engine that reads it. `scripts/install-skills.ps1` in the gandalf skill resolves the same path in a dev clone and in an installed ~/.agents/skills/ tree. `patches/manifest.json` records the verified diffs arming applies after install; see `patches/README.md`.

tiers.core: Every fleet. Relays, review pair, guards, the orchestrator and judging loadouts, UI evidence (palantír), and the browser backend it drives.
tiers.stack: On demand — only for repos that actually use the framework.
tiers.devops: On demand — only for repos with CI to harden.
tiers.optional: Deliberately outside the loop. Install when you want it: `security-review` for a security pass, `ui-review-loop` for a human-watches-video round.

order: Entries are listed in install order and in credits order. The delegate-skills entry must stay first: it ships the relays and the delegate-setup engine every --lane dispatch resolves through, so a user can choose their implementers before anything else is cast.
licenseNote: Entries marked `unverified` have not had their LICENSE checked yet. That is a to-do, not a claim — do not copy them into the README credits as if verified.

packs.name: Delegate Skills
packs.why: The relays that run implementers headlessly, plus delegate-setup — the engine every relay resolves --lane through. Installed first so the user can choose their implementers before the cast.

packs.name: Review Skills
packs.why: The two-lane diff debate and the PR babysitting loop. Its reviewer briefs are hardcoded and git-diff-bound, so the plan debate is ours instead (references/plan-debate.md).

packs.name: Guard Skills
packs.why: The judgment gates. They run in the orchestrator session on every diff — see references/gates.md.

packs.name: Ponytail
packs.why: The ladder philosophy behind 'the smallest change that works' — a rule of the road every code lane lives by.

packs.name: Superpowers
packs.install: npx skills add obra/superpowers -g -y -s systematic-debugging receiving-code-review writing-plans executing-plans verification-before-completion
packs.why: writing-plans shapes the plan Radagast attacks; systematic-debugging (bundling root-cause-tracing.md and defense-in-depth.md) and receiving-code-review arm the judging seats.

packs.name: Matt Pocock's Skills
packs.install: npx skills add mattpocock/skills -g -y -s grilling grill-with-docs to-tickets code-review domain-modeling diagnosing-bugs tdd codebase-design to-spec improve-codebase-architecture setup-pre-commit writing-for-agents wizard
packs.why: grilling interrogates the request until nothing is silently assumed; grill-with-docs wraps grilling + domain-modeling and persists answers to GLOSSARY.md and ADRs; domain-modeling invents the edge-case scenarios the judging seats hunt with. Note most of this pack is user-invoked (disable-model-invocation), so the preambles must NAME them — an unnamed skill is inert. grill-with-docs is user-invoked; Gandalf's automatic intake calls its two underlying skills directly.

packs.name: Palantír
packs.install: ships with this repo — installed by the council alongside gandalf and council-of-elrond
packs.why: OUR OWN child skill. UI verification through the page's own WebMCP tools plus the DOM timeline and the network HAR — structured evidence instead of a screenshot loop, with vision as ONE deliberate pass on appearance. Standalone: it does not depend on ui-review-loop at runtime, so it works where that skill is absent or its video half is broken. Derived from amElnagdy/ui-review-loop's recorder concept, credited above; re-shaped for a WebMCP-first, video-optional evidence model.

packs.name: Celebrimbor
packs.install: ships with this repo — installed by the council alongside gandalf and council-of-elrond
packs.why: OUR OWN child skill. The DESIGN.md forge: ensures the project has a current, validated DESIGN.md (Extract / Adopt / Generate / Normalize / Stitch modes) before the `ui` lane dispatches, so `ui` reads it first and `qa-look` judges against it. Methodology only — it draws on external methods when they are installed (VoltAgent/awesome-design-md, stitch-skills, ui-ux-pro-max, impeccable, ibelick/ui-skills) and validates with @google/design.md. Does not write product code and does not commit.

packs.name: UI Review Loop
packs.why: OPTIONAL, and not installed by default. Kept for the operator-watches-video case and for the coverage-audit methodology palantír was derived from. NOT the ui or qa lane's evidence path any more — palantir is. If you do install it, arming's patch step fixes its version gate and its silent video failure (patches/manifest.json).

packs.name: Agent Browser
packs.why: The browser backend palantír and ui-review-loop drive. Ships experimental WebMCP support ON by default for a locally launched Chrome (webmcp list/invoke/result/cancel), which is what palantir's tool-call evidence is built on. ffmpeg is a separate system dependency for recording.
